neighboring_unit_entries.title: A gamma-function ratio is even and increasing above a parameter threshold
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: A product representation makes F even, and logarithmic differentiation expresses its derivative with a sign that is positive for x>0 when the parameter exceeds one half. This supplies the monotonicity invoked when bounding the remainder integral.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: An integral-sign argument proves global decrease of the scaled gamma ratio
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: A gamma identity and product representation convert the logarithmic derivative of G into integral expressions. Two integrations by parts reduce its sign to positivity of a sine transform of a positive decreasing function, proving G decreases for x>0 when a>1; numerical computation suggests a lower threshold but is explicitly separate from the proof.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Scaling a gamma ratio and proving monotonicity makes an explicit remainder certificate possible, but the absolute monotone majorization discards oscillation and produces a coefficient that grows too early, explaining why the rigorous bound can be realistic for practical truncations yet useless near optimal truncation.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The source proposes oscillation-aware refinement but neither supplies it nor proves asymptoticity at optimal truncation.
